# dsh-attachment-cache
English | 中文
A sidebar panel for DeepSeek Harness that shows what is stored in `~/.dsh/attachments`, grouped by c
onversation, and lets you delete it deliberately — with a one-line explanation of what each deletion
breaks — or move the whole store to another disk without losing old conversations.
## Why this exists
Every image and file you attach to a conversation — and every image a tool hands back — is written t
o `~/.dsh/attachments/v1` as an immutable, content-addressed object (`objects/<sha256>` for normaliz
ed images, `file-objects/<sha256>` plus a `files/<sha256>/<name>` hardlink for files). The harness n
ever removes them: there is no garbage collector, no retention policy, no eviction. Quitting `dsh` d
oes not touch the folder either, so it only ever grows. A handful of conversations with TIFFs, PDFs
or screenshots can add gigabytes.
Nothing in DSH's UI tells you which conversation owns which bytes, or what happens if you delete a f
ile by hand. This plugin does.
## Features
- **Per-conversation inventory.** Every stored object mapped back to the conversations that referenc

e it, grouped by category (images, documents, other) with the owning message as the group title.
- *
*Explain-before-delete.** Selecting a row explains what the file is, how many conversations share it
, and exactly what stops working if it is removed — attachments are content-addressed, so one object

can serve many conversations.
- **Batch selection.** Per group (全选本组), per current filter (全选当前), o

r click-by-click, then one confirmed delete.
- **Unreferenced sweep.** Objects no session references

anymore are listed separately so you can reclaim them safely.
- **Derived-cache cleanup.** `~/.dsh/

cache/attachments` (request images) is regenerable; clear it whenever you like.
- **Storage relocati
on.** Copy the store to another disk, verify every digest, then swap the folder for an NTFS junction
— old conversations keep resolving because their references are content hashes, not paths. Three mo

des (move / keep a backup / switch to an existing store) and a one-click undo.
- **Read-only toward
sessions.** The panel never modifies session logs; it only reads them to learn which digest belongs
to which conversation.

## Using the panel
| Area | What it does |

| Tabs | `全部`, `图片`, `文档`, `其他`, `无引用` — each with a live count |
| Search | Matches file name, exte

nsion, or the conversation title that owns the file |
| Extension filter | Comma-separated suffixes,

e.g. `tif,pdf` |
| 全选当前 | Selects everything currently visible (including collapsed groups) |
| 展开全

部 / 收起全部 | Opens or folds every conversation card |
| 存储位置 | Opens the relocation dialog |
| 重新扫描 |

Re-reads the store and session logs |
| 删除选中 | Confirms, then deletes the selected objects |
Hovering a file shows its size, digest, share count and the consequence of deleting it; clicking pin
s it in the detail pane with a preview for PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP.
## What deletion actually breaks
| Deleted | Effect |
| An image object | That image no longer renders in every conversation that used it. Text and tool o

utput stay. |
| A file object | The original file can no longer be re-downloaded or re-read by a lat

er turn; the alias under `files/` disappears too. |
| A `files/<sha>/<name>` alias | Only that displ

ay name goes away; the object survives for other names. |
| `~/.dsh/cache/attachments` | Nothing per

manent — request images are regenerated on demand. |
| Unreferenced objects | Nothing; no session po

t images are regenerated on demand. |
| Unreferenced objects | Nothing; no session points at them. |
Deletion is permanent (no recycle bin), which is why the panel shows the impact first and asks once
more before removing anything.
## How it works
- **Host half** (`index.js`) registers routes under `/attachment-cache-manager`, guarded by the host

's connection fence, and reads:
- the attachment store (`objects`, `file-objects`, `files`, `request

-images`),
- session logs (`~/.dsh/sessions/<workspace>/<session>/session.v4.jsonl.zstd`, zstd multi

-frame) purely to map `sha256:<digest>` references to conversations.
- **Client half** (`client.js`)
registers a `sidebar.panellist` icon and a keyed `main` page; all visible text goes through the cli

ent locale.
- Deletions only happen through an explicit `POST /delete` after the confirmation dialog

nt locale.
- Deletions only happen through an explicit `POST /delete` after the confirmation dialog.
The plugin never calls into DSH's attachment service internals and never writes to session logs, so
a DSH update cannot corrupt the store through it.
## Compatibility

- DeepSeek Harness ≥ 0.2.1, `web` profile
- Node ≥ 20 (`zlib.zstdDecompress` for session logs)
- Win
dows 11 for storage relocation; browsing and deletion are platform-neutral
## Privacy
Everything is local. The panel reads files under `~/.dsh` and serves previews over the authenticated
localhost route of your own DSH instance; nothing is uploaded anywhere.
